subject: art-design
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which process describes shaping clay on a rotating potter's wheel?
options: Throwing
Casting
Carving
Welding
questions.explain: Throwing is the technique of forming clay vessels by hand on a spinning potter's wheel.

questions.q: What is a kiln used for when working with clay?
options: Firing clay at high temperature to harden it
Cooling clay quickly
Softening dried clay
Colouring clay with dye
questions.explain: A kiln fires ceramics at high temperatures, hardening the clay into a durable ceramic body.

questions.q: In sculpture, what is an armature?
options: An internal framework that supports modelling material
A tool for smoothing surfaces
A type of glaze finish
A moulding compound
questions.explain: An armature is a rigid internal skeleton, often of wire, that supports soft materials such as clay or plaster while modelling.

questions.q: Which process involves pouring a liquid material into a mould and letting it set?
options: Casting
Throwing
Whittling
Sanding
questions.explain: Casting fills a mould with a liquid material such as molten metal or plaster, which hardens into the mould's shape.

questions.q: Which technique is used to join two pieces of clay together securely?
options: Score and slip
Throw and centre
Glaze and fire
Sand and polish
questions.explain: Scoring the surfaces and applying slip (liquid clay) creates a strong bond between clay pieces.

questions.q: What best defines 'form' in three-dimensional design?
options: An element that has height, width and depth
A flat outline with only length and width
A single line drawn in space
The colour applied to a surface
questions.explain: Form is three-dimensional, possessing volume through height, width and depth, unlike a flat two-dimensional shape.

questions.q: What is a patina on a metal sculpture?
options: A surface colour or film that forms on or is applied to metal
A crack caused by overheating
A protective wooden base
A type of welding joint
questions.explain: A patina is a coloured surface layer on metal, formed naturally through weathering or applied deliberately as a finish.

questions.q: Carving a figure from a block of wood is an example of which kind of process?
options: Subtractive, because material is removed
Additive, because material is built up
Casting, because a mould is used
Assembling, because parts are joined
questions.explain: Carving is a subtractive process in which unwanted material is cut or chipped away to reveal the form.

questions.q: What is meant by 'negative space' in a three-dimensional work?
options: The empty space around and within a form
The heaviest part of the sculpture
The darkest painted area
The internal support structure
questions.explain: Negative space is the void surrounding and passing through a form, which artists use as an active part of the composition.

questions.q: How does a 'form' differ from a 'shape'?
options: Form is three-dimensional and has volume, while shape is two-dimensional
Form is always coloured, while shape is always plain
Form is smaller than shape
Form only exists in drawings, shape only in sculpture
questions.explain: A shape is a flat, enclosed area, whereas a form occupies real space with height, width and depth.

questions.q: Why might a designer make a maquette before producing a final sculpture?
options: To test ideas, proportions and structure on a small scale first
To replace the need for any final piece
To fire the clay more quickly
To add colour to the finished work
questions.explain: A maquette is a small preliminary model used to trial form, scale and construction before committing to the final work.

questions.q: Why is a clay object fired in a kiln rather than simply left to air-dry?
options: Firing permanently hardens the clay and makes it durable
Firing makes the clay softer and easier to reshape
Firing removes the need to glaze the object
Firing changes the clay back into liquid slip
questions.explain: Kiln firing causes irreversible chemical and physical changes that harden clay into strong, permanent ceramic.

questions.q: In three-dimensional design, what does 'scale' refer to?
options: The size of a form in relation to something else
The weight of the material used
The number of colours applied
The temperature of firing
questions.explain: Scale describes the relative size of a form compared with its surroundings, the viewer or other objects.

questions.q: Why is an armature important when modelling a tall clay or plaster figure?
options: It supports the material and stops the form from collapsing
It adds colour to the surface
It speeds up the drying process
It removes the need for firing
questions.explain: The armature provides internal structural support, preventing soft, heavy material from sagging or collapsing under its own weight.

questions.q: A student wants to model a slender, standing clay figure that keeps toppling over while soft. What should they use?
options: Build the figure around a wire armature
Fire the clay before modelling it
Apply a patina to the surface
Throw the figure on a wheel
questions.explain: A wire armature gives the tall, slender form the internal support it needs to stand while the clay remains soft.

questions.q: A designer needs to produce several identical copies of the same 3D form. Which process is most suitable?
options: Making a mould and casting each copy
Carving each copy separately from wood
Throwing each copy on the wheel
Applying a patina to each copy
questions.explain: Casting from a single mould reliably reproduces multiple identical copies of the same form.

questions.q: An artist wants the gaps and openings within their sculpture to be as important as the solid parts. Which concept are they working with?
options: Negative space
Patina
Subtractive carving
Slip casting
questions.explain: Deliberately using the voids and openings as a key compositional element means the artist is working with negative space.

questions.q: A student needs to attach a clay handle to a leather-hard clay mug so it will not fall off after firing. What should they do?
options: Score both surfaces and apply slip before joining
Press the pieces together while dry
Fire the mug and handle separately then glue them
Coat the join with patina
questions.explain: Scoring and slipping the joining surfaces fuses the handle to the mug so the bond survives drying and firing.

specSource: OCR GCSE (9–1) Art & Design (J170) specification; Three-Dimensional Design
